corrections.value: Black legged ticks, potential carriers of Lyme disease and Human Granulocytic Anaplasmosis, are common in Thousand Islands National Park. Check the 'Ticks and Your Health' page for protection tips.
corrections.quote: Black legged ticks, potential carriers of Lyme disease and Human Granulocytic Anaplasmosis, are common in Eastern Ontario and Thousand Islands National Park.
corrections.reason: The source specifically identifies the types of diseases carried by local ticks and provides a specific resource for health info.

corrections.value: Visit Mallorytown Landing, which features the Smoky Fire Trail and the Six Nations Trail (note: Six Nations Trail may be closed due to storm damage). View exhibits and obtain park permits from interpreters.
corrections.quote: There are also two trails at Mallorytown Landing – the Smoky Fire Trail (850 m), and the Six Nations Trail (1.1 km). ... The Six Nations Trail is closed due to damage from a recent and severe storm.
corrections.reason: Adds specific trail names and the current status of the Six Nations Trail found in the source.

summary: Thousand Islands National Park's geography as a riverfront archipelago and its accessibility requirements (boat-only for islands) are well-supported. Core trails and hubs like Mallorytown Landing, Jones Creek, and the Landons Bay Lookout are verified. Specific gateway cities and airport logistics are unverified. Seasonal closures are confirmed with a May reopening date.
